name: PT Fortune Mate Indonesia Tbk

frontmatter.title: Fortune Mate Indonesia - a Surabaya land bank priced for an appraisal nobody has filed
frontmatter.summary: We initiate FMII at SELL with a target of Rp58, -76.3% against the Rp244 price. The land is carried at cost, so our RNAV is book value by construction, and we weight it as a book multiple rather than an appraisal. The shares pay a premium to that book on a return below the cost of capital, with no dividend, and even the ceiling multiple the market has paid leaves the blend below the price.
thesis: The balance sheet is the business - 278 IDR bn of land under development plus 127 IDR bn of finished inventory, carried at cost, with no appraisal, NJOP reference or comparable land sale disclosed anywhere in the filings we could reach [S4].

The earnings base is disappearing - revenue falls to IDR10.6bn on our build against IDR32.0bn in FY2025, the half-year just filed shows a loss, and the fixed Surabaya overhead does not shrink with sales [S4][S5].
Half of the assets are stakes in unlisted property companies worth 311 IDR bn, not a development pipeline; no sale or valuation of either stake has been announced [S4].

The float is 11.8% against an exchange minimum of 15.0%, on IDR9.3m of three-month turnover; the house takes 30.0% off for that and the shares sit on the high-concentration list at 99.2% [S0][S9][S11].

The funding arithmetic is unforgiving - two related-party Bank Oke facilities, the term loan maturing in November 2026 and the revolver in June, against a run-rate that does not cover the fixed cost base, so the base case already assumes refinancing or an asset sale [S4][S5].

catalysts.event: Bank Oke facility maturity and any refinancing announcement
Q3-2026 unaudited financial statements due on the IR site
FY2026 audited statements, the first full year of the post-collapse run-rate

blocks.text: We initiate FMII at SELL with a twelve-month target of Rp58, -76.3% from the Rp244 last price, against a fundamental value of Rp82 before the liquidity haircut. The market capitalisation is IDR1,561.6bn for a company whose entire equity is IDR694.7bn, of which 311 IDR bn is a portfolio of minority stakes in unlisted property companies and the rest is Surabaya and Sidoarjo land carried at historical cost [S4].

Our variant view is not that the land is worthless - it is that the price already pays for a revaluation the company has never published. Struck at carrying cost, RNAV per share is book value per share, and we say so rather than present the result as an appraisal: the RNAV leg is book value at a discount, which is what most of the target is. The shares trade at 2.2x that book while earning 2.1% on it and paying no dividend [S0][S4]. To justify the price on our RNAV the parcels would have to be worth a multiple of their carrying value, and no appraisal, NJOP reference or arm's-length land sale in the filings supports it. The bull case now carries the uplift explicitly, marking the land above carrying and the stakes at book; it still lands at Rp102, below the price.

What moves the value is therefore narrow and identifiable. Up: a disclosed appraisal or a sale of the Sememi, Romokalisari, Tambak Sawah or Betro parcels above book, a buyer for the Masterin Property or Mitrakarya stakes at carrying value, or a resumption of land sales at the FY2025 margin. Down: another year at the filed half-year run-rate, a refinancing of the maturing facility on worse terms, or the free-float and concentration overhang forcing index-related supply. The scenario table in section five prices those paths; the base case is that none of the good ones happens on schedule.

FMII is a Surabaya-based landed-residential developer that has been in real estate since 2005, having previously manufactured shoes in Sidoarjo [S6][S2]. It reports a single real-estate development segment: the entire revenue line is land and building sales, with no rental, hotel or investment-property income [S4]. The company IR site lists audited statements from 2014 onward and quarterly filings back through the previous decade; there is no annual report narrative, no investor presentation and no sustainability report posted [S2][S3]. What we know about the business therefore comes from the statements themselves.

The asset base is a small portfolio of parcels in Surabaya and its Sidoarjo fringe. At the last balance sheet the company carried 278 IDR bn of land under development (Tambak Sawah, Betro, Romokalisari and Tambak Osowilangun), 127 IDR bn of inventory ready for sale (Sememi and Romokalisari in Surabaya, Tambak Sawah and Betro in Sidoarjo) and 90.2 IDR bn of buildings under construction [S4]. Sales are recognised on transfer rather than on progress, which is why the revenue line is lumpy and why customer advances are a better near-term indicator than any backlog: sales advances fell to 9.0 IDR bn at end-2025 from a materially higher balance a year earlier [S4].

Beside the land sits the part of the balance sheet the market rarely looks at. FMII owns 49.4% of PT Masterin Property, carried under the equity method at 258 IDR bn, and 18.0% of PT Mitrakarya Multiguna at cost, 53.1 IDR bn; together 311 IDR bn of stock investment against total equity of 695 IDR bn [S4]. Neither stake is listed, neither produces a disclosed cash return, and the equity-method result was a small loss in the year [S4]. They are the single largest reason a buyer might argue the shares are cheap, and equally the reason the balance sheet tells you little about what the assets are worth.

Strategy, in as much as the filings disclose one, is realisation rather than growth. The company buys no land, launches no township and spends essentially nothing on fixed assets - capital expenditure was immaterial against revenue in each of the last two years [S4]. Its competitive position is that of a sub-scale, single-city, family-controlled challenger: revenue of IDR32.0bn puts it far below the listed national developers in the same sector, and its advantage, if any, is land on the books at costs set years ago rather than brand, scale or access to capital [S4].

Control is concentrated and has been stable. PT Surya Mega Investindo holds 46.7% of the shares, and with two individual holdings alongside it the insider block is 87.9% [S4][S0]. The same group stands behind the company bank: PT Bank Oke Indonesia is a related party, holds part of FMII cash and is the lender under both the working-capital revolver and the term facility, with PT Surya Mega Investindo as corporate guarantor [S4]. That is the structure a minority holder has to underwrite, and we return to it in section six.

The Indonesian landed-housing market FMII sells into is contracting. Bank Indonesia survey data show primary residential sales falling 8.4% year on year in Q3-2026 while the residential price index rose only 0.6%, and the developers association expects no recovery before 2027 [S8]. The mechanism is familiar and rate-driven: purchasing power is weak, construction costs are up and mortgage rates remain high, so volumes fall while prices are sticky downward [S7][S8]. For a seller of finished houses and serviced land in the Surabaya fringe, that combination is worse than a price correction, because it means the inventory does not clear at any volume.

Our house macro stance is consistent with that read. The macro deck carries a balance-of-payments-pressure regime and a cautious tilt, and the desk treats Indonesian rate-sensitive property as an avoid: policy rates held steady through the autumn, and the transmission to mortgage pricing is what determines whether landed demand recovers [S7][S8]. We have not assumed that a rate cut rescues volumes in our base case; the forecast holds revenue flat after the current year for exactly that reason.

Regulation cuts both ways for a name this small. The exchange raised the minimum free float for continued listing to 15.0% of listed shares in March 2026, a rule that binds precisely the companies with family blocks like this one [S9]. Separately, the exchange high-shareholding-concentration review now covers hundreds of issuers and FMII was added to it in November 2026 with a concentration measure of 99.2% [S11][S10]. Being on that list does not delist a company, but it does attach liquidity and index-treatment consequences to a stock whose free float is already 11.8% [S0][S9]. For a holder, the practical effect is that entry and exit happen in a thin market, which is why the house method applies a liquidity discount before arriving at a target.

Competitive structure in the sub-market is fragmented and local. There is no published market-share series for the Sidoarjo fringe, so we cannot quantify FMII share; what we can say is that its revenue of IDR32.0bn is small enough that its pricing is a follower, not a leader [S4][S8]. On the five forces: buyer power is high because the buyer can wait or buy a competitor unit; supplier power sits with contractors and land owners rather than with FMII, which already owns its land; the threat of new entrants is high in a market where any local developer can assemble a parcel; substitutes are second-hand houses and rental; and rivalry is intense, with the contraction in volumes pushing developers to discount. FMII durable advantage is the cost basis of land bought long ago - a moat that shows up in the gross margin and nowhere else.

The external influences we monitor are the policy rate path and mortgage pricing, construction cost inflation, and the purchasing-power squeeze that shows up directly in the survey data [S7][S8]. Currency is not a first-order exposure here: the debt is rupiah-denominated and the revenue domestic [S4]. Land regulation in East Java and any change to the treatment of land banks in the tax base would matter more, and neither is disclosed in the filings we hold.

The five-year record is one of a business shrinking while staying comfortably profitable. Revenue ran from IDR52.4bn in FY2022 to IDR32.0bn in FY2025, a decline of -9.3% in the last year after -17.1% the year before, while the gross margin held between 59.6% in the weaker year and 76.1% in the strong one [S4]. Net profit attributable to owners was IDR14.5bn, an EBITDA margin of 49.8% and a return on equity of 2.1% [S4]. The high margins are the signature of land sold from an old cost base, not of pricing power: when the mix moves to newer, costlier units the margin falls with it.

The half-year just filed changes the picture. Revenue of 5.3 IDR bn against the whole of the prior financial year in the comparable half, and a net loss of -1.3 IDR bn, with selling and administrative cost of roughly the same absolute size as before [S5]. Because the overhead is fixed and the revenue base is not, our model carries operating cost at 66.3% of the new revenue line - the same absolute cost as the filed half, re-expressed as a ratio - which is why the forecast EBITDA margin of -1.8% compresses against the 49.8% earned last year. The gross margin we use is 60.0%, deliberately between the audited three-year average and the weaker margin realised in the half-year, because the mix that produced the FY2025 peak is not repeatable [S4][S5].

The revenue build is simple, and its one judgement should be labelled as one. FMII discloses no marketing-sales KPI, so the driver is development revenue itself, and our FY2026E line of IDR10.6bn is exactly the annualisation of the filed half-year - -66.9% against FY2025, and flat thereafter in nominal terms [S5][S8]. The annualisation is a judgement, not a forecast the company has given: doubling a half-year assumes the second half repeats a first half that itself fell at the fastest rate in the record, and the one disclosed forward indicator points lower, because sales advances were 9.0 IDR bn at the last audited year-end against a far larger balance a year earlier [S4]. We carry the annualisation because a half-year is the only run-rate we can observe, and section five's bear case is the honest alternative. There is no recurring line: the only non-development inflow in the financial statements is a prepaid income - rent balance of 0.4 IDR bn, which is a liability for rent received in advance rather than revenue, and we model recurring revenue as nil [S4].

Tax is the rate the filings show being paid, 5.6% of pre-tax profit, consistent with the final income tax on land and building transfers rather than the headline corporate rate [S4]. D&A is immaterial (IDR0.5bn) because the fixed-asset base is a rounding error, and capital expenditure is held near zero, as it has been [S4]. Working capital is the land itself: we hold operating working capital at the reported absolute stock of about IDR155.8bn rather than letting the engine ratio release it as sales fall, because inventory does not disappear when houses go unsold [S0]. That is a stated choice with a stated cost: holding roughly IDR155.8bn of working capital against a IDR10.6bn revenue line is what turns a profitable year into a working-capital-absorbing one, and it is the reason free cash flow to equity stays thin (IDR0.3bn in FY2026E) while the model funds the gap with IDR5.5bn of annual borrowing. Debt therefore rises from IDR50.5bn to IDR78.0bn by FY2030E. It passes the IDR58.0bn term-loan ceiling in FY2027E, at IDR61.5bn, but stays inside the committed capacity of the two Bank Oke facilities taken together, which is at least 58.0 IDR bn plus 20.0 IDR bn [S4]. There is no funding plug in the template; the thin cash path (IDR-2.5bn by FY2030E) is the arithmetic signal that the term loan has to be renewed, enlarged or replaced by an asset sale.

Debt is modest in absolute terms and entirely rupiah: 40.0 IDR bn of current bank loans plus a long-term portion, against cash of 1.6 IDR bn and equity of 695 IDR bn, for net debt of IDR48.9bn [S4]. It sits on two related-party facilities, and they should not be run together. The fixed term loan is IDR58.0bn at a contractual 10.0%, maturing 22 November 2026; the revolving current account is IDR20.0bn at the same rate, renewed to 26 June 2026; both are secured on the same two Tambakrejo parcels, one held by the company and one by an affiliate, under a guarantee from the controlling shareholder, and IDR40.0bn was drawn against them at the last year-end [S4]. The interest charge deserves a word. The contractual rate is 10.0%, but the FY2025 profit and loss shows almost no interest because borrowing costs are capitalised into land under development, as the non-cash activities note states [S4]. We choose to book the contractual charge of IDR5.0bn in the profit and loss line so the cash cost is visible; that is a deliberate reporting choice, and it is why the forecast loss (IDR-5.7bn) is wider than an annualisation of the filed half-year. The alternative - capitalising as the company does - would flatter the forecast loss and change nothing in the valuation, which is struck off the June-2026 balance sheet and does not capitalise a profit line.

On capital allocation the record is consistent: no dividend has ever been paid (Rp0 trailing dividend, payout of 0.0%) and profit has been retained, which is why book value has crept up while the share count stayed at 6,400 m shares [S0][S4]. Management has not bought back stock, issued shares or sold assets in the period we reviewed.

On earnings quality, three flags carry weight and none is manipulation-class. First, cash conversion is weak: net profit of IDR14.5bn was earned in a year when operating cash flow was negative [S4], the signature of land-sale profit recognised ahead of collection. Second, the revenue base depends on a handful of transactions, so a single parcel decides the year. Third, the related-party gravity is real but disclosed: cash at the related-party bank, borrowings from it, payables to group companies including PT Gozcoland Development, and a guarantee from the controlling shareholder [S4]. There is no going-concern notation, no equity deficit and no late filing in the period; the filings history on the IR site does show statements from earlier years only published in 2023, which we treat as a disclosure-cadence flag rather than a current one [S3].

We value FMII on RNAV as the primary method because the company is a balance sheet of land and minority stakes, not an earnings stream: its profit is whatever parcel transferred that year, so a multiple on earnings is a bet on the mix rather than on the company. The build is unglamorous, and it has one property we state before using it. The land is carried at cost; no appraisal of the Sememi, Romokalisari, Tambak Sawah, Betro or Osowilangun parcels exists in the filings or on the IR site, and no arm's-length land sale is disclosed [S4][S2]. We take the operating asset base - current real estate assets of 124 IDR bn plus land under development of 268 IDR bn at the June balance sheet, the land-acquisition advances of 40.6 IDR bn and the small residual operating assets, net of the non-debt liabilities that fund them - add the 311 IDR bn stock investment (within a rounding error of its June figure) and deduct net debt and minorities, every item dated 30 June 2026 [S5][S4]. Because that base is the residual of the same balance sheet, RNAV per share comes back to parent book value per share almost exactly. The 80.0% RNAV leg is therefore, in plain terms, book value at a discount, and the blended target is mostly a book-multiple target. We label it that way rather than dressing carrying cost up as an asset value.

The discount is 40.0%, and it needs the same candour. The peer band for Indonesian developers is measured against *appraised* NAVs; applied to a cost base the same rate is the deepest discount in that set, not the mild end, and this company's own four observed year-end P/BV readings never once put book value at a discount at all. The shares have paid a premium to this book for four years, which is itself evidence that the land is worth more than cost. We keep the discount anyway for a stated reason: with no appraisal, it does double duty, standing in both for the missing mark and for the illiquidity and governance of a 11.8% float. The price at Rp244 is several times this RNAV, so the comparison with the peer band is inverted - buyers here pay a premium, not a discount. On the RNAV leg as struck the shares are worth Rp65.

The cost of capital is a cross-check rather than a driver, because the DCF is not a weighted method. The table above sets out the build: a rupiah risk-free rate, a mature-market equity risk premium, a country premium, a thin beta, and a debt weight of 2.8% because the capital structure is overwhelmingly equity (97.2%). The resulting cost of equity is 12.0% and the WACC 11.9%.

sets out the cash-flow path: revenue flat at the current run-rate, nil capex, a held inventory balance and the contractual interest charge. The DCF lands well below RNAV, which is the correct signal for a business consuming rather than compounding its asset base. We do not weight it.

The cross-checks are where the disagreement sits, and the weights now say which one we believe. The P/E leg uses 13.8x: FMII's own history contains one year inside the sane band, so the engine falls back to the peer median rather than printing a multiple set in a period when this stock traded at a triple-digit earnings multiple [S0]. Applied to FY2025 earnings of IDR14.5bn it gives Rp31, -51.7% against the RNAV leg - lower, because a P/E capitalises a shrinking, lumpy earnings stream while RNAV capitalises the asset that produces it.

The P/BV leg is the ceiling, and it is a distant one: 3.0x on book equity of IDR694.7bn gives Rp325, 399.9% above the RNAV leg. That multiple is the mean of the last four year-end readings, every one of which put book value at a premium - including the highest, set in the year after the 2023 exchange suspension - and it is several times the peer median we carry for the sector. It was not earned on a superior return: return on equity was 2.6%, 1.5% and 2.1% in the three audited years to FY2025, the year before was in the same low range [S0], and the figure drifts with the size of the parcel sold rather than improving, never covering the cost of equity [S4]. A multiple several times the peer median on a return below the risk-free rate is what a thin float can make the market pay, not a fair value. We keep it at a 5.0% weight as a stated ceiling; because it is worth several times the RNAV leg it still supplies more of the blend than its weight implies, and the table lets the reader see exactly that. Drop the leg and the target is lower, not higher.
The sensitivity grid needs the same honesty.

varies the RNAV discount against presales growth, and every row is flat across the growth axis. That is not an error but the point: none of the three weighted methods capitalises forecast revenue, so no plausible sales path moves the target, and the grid is there as a control. What moves the value is the mark on the land, which the scenario table carries in both tails. We ran that ladder from half to triple carrying value, and even at triple carrying the target stays below Rp244: the 30.0% house liquidity haircut sits on top of whatever the parcels are worth, and the price needs a mark on the stakes as well as the land that no filing supports.
The haircut is where the float bites. Three-month turnover is IDR9.3m on a 11.8% free float, so the house applies 30.0% before setting a target; that takes Rp82 to Rp58 [S0][S9].

What the price implies is worth stating, because the engine cannot print it. The reverse-DCF on presales growth does not bracket Rp244 - no sales path reaches it, because growth cannot make a land bank worth a multiple of its carrying cost by selling one parcel at a time. What the price implies is a revaluation of the parcels, or of the investment stakes, that no filing supports. That is the case against us in its strongest form, and it is real: if an appraisal exists and is published above carrying value, our RNAV is too low by the full amount of the uplift and the shares are not expensive. It is also why Rp58 must be read for what it is - a fundamental value struck on today's disclosures, not a forecast of where the price trades in twelve months. The mechanism that closes the gap is in section five; the timing is not something the filings let us date.

Bear, base and bull carry probabilities of 25.0%, 50.0% and 25.0%, and this time the shocks do work on the value. Both tails move the same four drivers in opposite directions, as the table prints them: the sales path and the gross margin move the earnings, the RNAV discount moves the market's mark, and the land bank is re-marked at a multiple of carrying. The bear takes the land below carrying - a seller in a contracting market accepts less than book for the Sememi, Romokalisari and Betro parcels - widens the discount, and pushes revenue below the filed half-year run-rate; it is worth Rp59 before the roll-forward. The bull takes the land to a modest premium to carrying, the smallest mark that makes the asset case arithmetic rather than assertion, recovers part of the collapse in revenue, returns the margin toward the FY2025 peak and narrows the discount; it is worth Rp91. The asymmetry is not manufactured: the bull is the mirror of the bear on every driver, and on the operating ones we have no sourced reason to weight the downside more heavily. What the table does show is the range: even at Rp102 the bull case does not reach Rp244.
The risks that matter, in order of what would change the view:

items: Liquidity and float (high likelihood, high impact). A 11.8% float against a
15.0% exchange minimum, IDR9.3m of three-month turnover and a place on
the high-concentration list at 99.2% [S0][S9][S11]. Closing the gap to the minimum means
placing stock worth many times a day's turnover; on the three-month average that is decades of
continuous dealing, so any placement arrives at a discount and the 30.0%
haircut is the quantification. Since 13 November 2026 the high-concentration names are outside the
IHSG calculation [S10], removing index demand from an already thin register, and the exchange is
explicit that the status is not a finding of wrongdoing [S10].
Refinancing (medium likelihood, high impact). Two related-party facilities, not one: a
IDR58.0bn term loan maturing 22 November 2026 and a IDR20.0bn current-account
revolver renewed to 26 June 2026, both secured on the same Tambakrejo parcels under the same
corporate guarantee, with IDR40.0bn drawn against them at the last year-end [S4].
Committed capacity is at least the sum of the two, so total debt passing the term-loan ceiling is
not a breach - our modelled debt does that in FY2027E, at IDR61.5bn - and the risk
is renewal on worse terms, or no renewal, for a borrower whose run-rate does not cover its fixed
cost base [S5].
Demand (high likelihood, medium impact). Primary residential sales are still falling and recovery is
expected only in 2027; a further year at the filed half-year run-rate is the base case, and a worse
one is the bear [S8][S7].
Concentration and governance (medium likelihood, medium impact). An insider block of
87.9%, related-party banking, related-party payables and guarantees to the
controlling shareholder leave minority holders with little influence over asset-sale timing or terms
Dilution (low likelihood, high impact, outside the scenario maths). Authorised capital is
6,400 m shares issued against a much larger authorised pool [S4]. If the facilities are not renewed on
workable terms, a discounted rights issue to the controlling group is the obvious funding route. We
do not put it in the bear case because the engine applies one share count to all three methods, so a
share shock would not flow through to value; we state it instead. A placement at a discount cuts
per-share value one for one and would hit the RNAV per share and both earnings legs together.
Accounting (low likelihood, medium impact). Borrowing costs capitalised into inventory and revenue
recognised on a handful of transfers mean reported profit can lead cash by a wide margin [S4].

blocks.text: Signposts that would change the view: a published appraisal or a land sale above carrying value; a buyer for either unlisted stake at or near book; a refinancing of the term loan on terms no worse than the current agreement; two consecutive quarters of revenue above the filed half-year run-rate; and any move by the controlling shareholder to raise the free float.

Ownership is the centre of gravity. PT Surya Mega Investindo holds 46.7%, two named individuals hold the same stake each, and the block is 87.9% of the register against a free float of 11.8% [S4][S0]. The same controlling shareholder guarantees the company bank facility, and the lender, PT Bank Oke Indonesia, is a related party that also holds part of FMII cash [S4]. Related-party payables include group companies [S4]. We did not find a pledge of the controlling stake disclosed in the audited statements; if one exists outside them it is margin-call supply waiting to happen.

The disclosure record is mixed. The IR site carries the audited statements back to 2014, the last five years of quarterly filings and the AGM materials, which is better than many small caps [S3]. But several earlier-year statements were only published in 2023, years after their periods, and no annual report narrative, presentation or sustainability report is posted [S2][S3]. The shares were suspended by the exchange in 2023 for a cumulative price surge, a cooling-down action rather than a sanction, but a reminder that this is a stock that can move violently on little information [S6].

Dividends have never been paid: trailing DPS is Rp0 and the payout ratio is 0.0% in every year we hold [S0][S4]. Retention is defensible while the company is funding land development, but with a return on equity of 2.1% it is not creating value for a minority holder who cannot sell at a fair price.

On ESG, the exposures are the standard ones for a small Indonesian developer: land-title and permitting risk in East Java, drainage and flood exposure in the Surabaya delta, labour practices at contractors, and the absence of any published policy or target. There is no sustainability disclosure on the IR site to assess [S2]. We do not score it as a differentiator; we treat the absence of disclosure as a governance data point.

Small Indonesian developers of this kind often sit inside a family group that also owns a bank or a finance
company, and the bank becomes both the lender and the deposit-taker for the developer. The structure is
legal and common, but it means the board ability to negotiate borrowing terms at arm length is limited, and
minority holders should read the related-party note before the income statement.

The dated events are narrow and known. The Bank Oke facility matures in November 2026 and any refinancing announcement is the single most important near-term disclosure [S4]. The Q3-2026 unaudited statements are due on the IR site by the end of November and will show whether the second half repeats the filed half-year run-rate [S3]. The FY2026 audited statements, due in March 2027, are the first full year of the post-collapse economics and will settle the margin and the inventory-consumption question [S3]. The exchange's 15.0% free-float minimum binds the register from March 2026 onward [S9]; we hold no dated compliance deadline for this issuer's tier in the filings and exchange material we can cite, so we treat any placement as an event risk rather than date it.

Between updates we watch: quarterly revenue against twice the filed half-year; sales advances, which lead transfers; the split of inventory between land under development and finished stock, because a shift to finished stock means unsold houses; the equity-method result from the Masterin Property stake, the only mark-to-market proxy we have for the investments; the cash balance against the facility path; and any appraisal, sale or pledge disclosure touching the land bank or the investment stakes [S4].

bear.narrative: The 2026 sales collapse is not a timing gap but the end of the saleable frontage: revenue stays near the 1H2026 run-rate and falls further, the 60% gross margin gives way to 55% as the cheap Tambak Sawah and Betro parcels are exhausted, the Rp58bn Bank Oke facility is not replaced on the same terms when it matures in November 2026, and the market keeps applying a wider discount to unappraised Surabaya land. Housing demand keeps contracting and recovery slips past 2027.

bull.narrative: The mirror case: the 1H2026 lull is a release-timing gap in a lumpy land-sale business and a second-half sale plus a better mix restores revenue toward the FY2025 level, gross margin returns to the FY2025 76% as the low-cost parcels are sold, and the discount to RNAV narrows as the market recognises that Rp432bn of Sidoarjo and Surabaya land sits on the books at historical cost with Rp311bn of unlisted property stakes beside it. A sale of the Masterin Property or Mitrakarya stakes at book would crystallise the asset case.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs presales growth and RNAV discount

assumptions.label: Presales growth
assumptions.basis: The driver is development revenue because FMII discloses no marketing-sales (presales) KPI and the LK contains no presales note [S4]. FY2026E is set from the visible run-rate: 1H2026 net sales were Rp5.30bn against Rp32.03bn in 1H2025, i.e. the whole of FY2025 was booked in the first half of last year and the first half of this year is 83% lower [S5, F22]; doubling 1H2026 gives Rp10.60bn, a 66.9% fall. FY2027E-FY2030E are held flat in nominal terms: no launch pipeline, land acquisition or presales target is disclosed, the company has no debt headroom beyond the Rp58bn Bank Oke facility maturing November 2026 [S4, F25], and the national market is contracting (primary residential sales -8.43% yoy in Q3-2026, transactions decelerating, recovery expected only in 2027) [S8][S7]. Flat is the more probable path than recovery; no decline is assumed either.

assumptions.label: Share of presales recognised in the same year
assumptions.basis: FMII sells land and finished houses and recognises revenue at the sale: there is no progress- based high-rise revenue and no disclosed backlog, and customer deposits (sales advances) fell to Rp8.99bn at end-2025 from Rp30.59bn a year earlier [S4, F20], so there is almost no carried balance to recognise in a later year. Same-year recognition of the sales line is therefore the accurate treatment.

assumptions.label: Recurring revenue growth
assumptions.basis: There is no recurring business: no investment property, no mall, hotel or rental line in the revenue note, and the entire Rp32.03bn of FY2025 revenue is land and building sales [S4, F2]. The only non-development balance the filings disclose is prepaid income - rent of Rp405.8m at 31 Dec 2025 (F27), which note 19 shows as a current LIABILITY for rent received in advance, not revenue [S4]. The template's recurring line starts at that balance, so FY2026E growth is set to -100% to extinguish it: the forecast revenue build carries no rent at all and the capitalised recurring value is zero because the recurring margin is zero. Later years are zero on a zero base.

assumptions.label: Development gross margin
assumptions.basis: The audited three-year average is 68.6% (FY2023A 70.2%, FY2024A 59.6%, FY2025A 76.1% on revenue 32.03 and cost of sales 7.67, F3/F5) and the current year realised margin is 44.2% (1H2026 gross profit Rp2.34bn on Rp5.30bn of sales, S5). Margin depends entirely on which parcel is sold: the old Tambak Sawah and Betro land carries a very low cost base, while the more recent Palm Residence and Palm Oasis units do not. 60% sits between the three-year audited average and the current-year realised mix, so it neither extrapolates the FY2025 peak nor the 1H2026 trough.

assumptions.label: Recurring gross margin
assumptions.basis: No recurring revenue exists (no investment property or rental line in the LK, all revenue is land and building sales, S4/F2), so the recurring gross margin is zero by construction and does not move the capitalised recurring value.

assumptions.label: Cap rate for investment property (RNAV)
assumptions.basis: Inert: FMII owns no investment property and books no recurring revenue (S4 balance sheet and revenue note), so the capitalised recurring business is zero whatever rate is used. 0.09 is the mid-point of the 8-10% Indonesian commercial NOI band the desk uses for developer peers and is stated in the report as a non-driver.

assumptions.label: Target discount to RNAV
assumptions.basis: IDX developers trade at persistent discounts to RNAV (method card), but that band is measured against APPRAISED NAVs. Applied to a cost base the same 40% is the deepest discount in the peer set, not the mild end, and this company's own four year-end P/BV readings never put book value at a discount at all [S0, S4]: the shares have paid a premium to cost-based book for four years. We keep 40% for one reason, stated in section 4: with no appraisal the discount does double duty, standing in both for the missing mark and for the illiquidity and governance of an 11.75% float, and the house also takes a separate 30% liquidity haircut afterwards. It is not calibrated to the price - the shares trade at a multiple of this RNAV, so the peer comparison is inverted - and the bear and bull scenarios move it in both directions (50% / 30%) so the reader can see the band.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: G&A is fixed, not proportional: 1H2026 selling and general-and-administrative expense was Rp3,509.5m (Rp53.0m selling plus Rp3,456.5m G&A) on Rp5,295.2m of sales, i.e. 66.3% of revenue [S5]; FY2025 was Rp8,877.9m on Rp32,025.6m (27.7%) [S4]. With revenue held at the 1H2026 annualised level the ratio is 66.3%, which keeps the absolute cost at the last actual rather than letting a shrinking sales line shrink a fixed cost base. It is a cost-level assumption, not a margin call. The choice is worth stating: it is the last actual cost in money terms, so the forecast loss is the fixed overhead of a company that has lost two thirds of its sales.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Held at the last actual absolute charge rather than the historical ratio: FY2025 D&A was Rp0.483bn (S0) on revenue of Rp32.03bn, so 1.5%, but revenue now runs at Rp10.60bn and D&A does not fall with it. 0.0455 re-prices the same Rp0.483bn against the new revenue base. The asset base is tiny (net fixed assets Rp0.46bn, S4), so the line is immaterial to value either way.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Maintenance only: FY2025 capital expenditure was Rp1.60m against Rp32.03bn of revenue (0.005%) and FY2024 was Rp0.95m [S4 cash flow]. The company buys no land and starts no new township; land for development is already on the balance sheet at cost. 0.05% keeps capex at the last actual absolute level (about Rp5m) on the smaller revenue base.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Working capital here is the land and building inventory, not trade credit: the pack's operating working capital was Rp155.8bn against Rp32.0bn of sales at end-2025 [S0, F7, F8], essentially the real-estate inventory net of payables and sales advances. The ratio 14.7 is calibrated to hold that absolute stock against the new Rp10.6bn revenue base (155.8 / 10.6), so the forecast carries the same rupiah of inventory as the last actual. The engine default of 1.5x would cut working capital to about Rp16bn and release more than Rp130bn of cash on a sales decline, which no balance sheet can do - land does not disappear because the houses were not sold. The choice has a stated cost: it is why free cash flow to equity stays thin and debt rises to fund it, and it is the reason the model, not the market, shows the refinancing need.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Final income tax on land and building transfers, which is what the LK shows being paid: Rp0.859bn of tax on Rp15.395bn of pre-tax profit in FY2025 (5.58%) and Rp0.651bn on Rp11.016bn in FY2024 (5.91%) [S4]. The rate is a flat final tax on gross sales rather than the 22% corporate rate, so it is held at the FY2025 effective rate.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: Both Bank Oke Indonesia facilities carry a contractual 10% per annum: the Rp58bn term loan (Agreement No. 61, maturing 22 November 2026, F25) and the Rp20bn current-account revolver (F31), the two secured on the same Tambakrejo parcels with a guarantee from PT Surya Mega Investindo [S4]. The engine default of 3% is an artefact of a tiny absolute interest charge in a year when borrowing costs were capitalised; the contractual 10% is the rate that refinances. The resulting P&L charge of about Rp5.0bn a year is a stated choice - the LK capitalises borrowing costs into land under development (non-cash activities note) - it widens the forecast loss and does not touch the target, which is struck off the June balance sheet.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: Engine default kept: FY2025 interest income was Rp32.05m on Rp1.59bn of cash (2.0%), but the cash sits partly at the related-party bank that lends to the company, so the observed yield is the right anchor and the amount is immaterial (1.6bn against 694bn of equity).

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: The run-rate does not fund itself and the model carries no funding plug, so the deficit is shown as borrowing: with revenue at Rp11.0bn the gross profit covers Rp6.6bn of the Rp7.3bn selling and G&A base and Rp5.0bn of contractual interest at 10% on the Rp50.5bn drawn balance [S4, S5, F18], leaving a Rp5.5bn annual gap. That is a deliberate, adverse choice: the LK capitalises borrowing costs into land under development (note 39 non-cash activities, S4), which is why the P&L interest charge was only Rp42.5m in FY2025 while the cash cost is real. Showing it as borrowing makes the funding need visible: debt reaches about Rp78bn by FY2030E against the Rp58bn Bank Oke facility limit that matures 22 November 2026 [S4, F25], so the base case already assumes a refinancing or the sale of part of the Rp311bn investment stake. It does not change the target, which is struck off the June-2026 balance sheet, but it is the arithmetic a holder has to believe. FY2031E onward carries the same rate of borrowing.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: No recurring non-operating line: the FY2025 'other income - net' of Rp263.4m and the 1H2026 figure of Rp193.1m are interest and sundry items already inside the financial lines, and there is no associate contribution of any size (share of the Masterin Property result was a Rp0.49m loss) [S4].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Negligible: non-controlling interest on the balance sheet is Rp0.285bn against Rp694.7bn of total equity and the minority share of profit is under Rp0.5m a year [S4]. Set to zero for the forecast; the RNAV deduction uses the balance-sheet minority as reported.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Nil, and it has never paid: no dividend appears in the price history (S0 DPS zero in FY2022-FY2025) and retained earnings rose by exactly the year's profit (Rp45.99bn unappropriated at end-2025 against Rp31.46bn at end-2024) [S4]. There is no dividend policy on the IR site [S2]. A 2.1% ROE on a 12% free float gives no reason to expect a payout to start.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: No issue assumed. Authorised capital was raised to 25bn shares in November 2023 but the issued count has been 6.4bn since, unchanged in FY2025 and 1H2026 [S4, F19], so the company retains a multiple of its issued capital in headroom. A discounted rights issue is a live funding route if the facilities are not renewed. It is NOT modelled as a scenario shock: the engine applies a single share count to all three valuation methods, so a share-count shock would not flow through to the target and would misrepresent the maths. It is disclosed in section 5 as a stated risk outside the scenario arithmetic, with the per-share effect noted.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Zero: the company is liquidating a fixed land bank at a slow pace with no land acquisition, no launch pipeline and sales contracting (1H2026 revenue -83% yoy, S5; national primary sales -8.43% yoy in Q3-2026, S8). It is not a going-concern compounder. The DCF is not a weighted method here, so the rate affects only the cross-check.

challenges.challenge: The engine's RNAV is book value by construction: landbank_value is set as total assets 758.61 less cash 1.59 less investments 311.42 less non-debt liabilities 13.41, so RNAV = total assets - total liabilities - minority = parent equity (699.67 against 694.45). The asset value therefore contains no land work at all and any landbank input built this way cancels; the Rp66 RNAV leg is a P/BV at 0.6x. The report calls the result almost exactly book, hiding that it is exact by algebra.
challenges.answer: Rebuilt landbank_value on the 30-Jun-2026 balance sheet (TA 747.48 less cash 1.60 less investments 311.42 less non-debt liabilities 9.06 = 425.4) and stated in section 4 that at carrying cost RNAV equals parent book by construction, so the 80% RNAV leg is book value at a discount, not an appraisal; the three valuation legs are shown with value and weight so the reader sees the book-multiple basis [S5][S4].

challenges.challenge: Date splice: landbank 432.2 and the 13.41 non-debt liabilities are 31-Dec-2025 (S4), while net debt 43.67, minority 0.28 and book 693.15 are 30-Jun-2026 (datapack latest_bs). RNAV 699.67 is therefore Rp5.2bn above 31-Dec-2025 parent equity (694.45) and Rp6.8bn above 30-Jun-2026 (692.87), purely from using June net debt against December assets, and the report both says the target is struck off June-2026 and that RNAV equals book.
challenges.answer: Date splice removed: landbank 425.4 is built from the June-2026 total assets and non-debt liabilities, so assets, net debt, minorities and book all share 30 June 2026; the landbank_basis states the construct and §4 says every item is dated the same day [S5][S4].

challenges.challenge: The 40% RNAV discount is justified as the mild end of the band, but the peer band (15-86%: CTRA 0.55, BSDE 0.65, PWON 0.72, LPKR 0.71) is measured against APPRAISED NAV. Applied to carrying cost, 40% is deeper than any peer's and the stated reason is backwards: an unmarked base plus a mild discount is not mild, it is the most conservative point in the set. The name's own discount band, which the method card requires, is not computed; price is at a 123% premium to this RNAV.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now says the peer band is measured on appraised NAVs, that the same 40% applied to cost is the deepest discount in the set (not the mild end), that FMII's own four year-end readings never put book at a discount, and that the price/RNAV comparison is inverted at a premium; we keep 40% as a stated double-duty discount and move it 30/50% in the scenarios [S0][S4].

challenges.challenge: The 60% RNAV weight is nominal, not effective: 0.6 x 65.59 = 39.4 of the 110.6 blend (36%), while the P/BV leg contributes 64.9 (59%) and the P/E leg 6.3. The report says RNAV is the primary method and that the P/BV leg is a ceiling rather than fair value, yet the leg the analyst disowns supplies most of the target. A reader cannot see from section 4 that the target is mainly a 3.0x book target.
challenges.answer: Reweighted to RNAV 0.80 / P/E 0.15 / P/BV 0.05 and section 4 states that the P/BV leg still supplies more of the blend than its weight because it is worth several times the RNAV leg, that readers can see it in the table, and that dropping the leg lowers the target further rather than raising it [S0][S4].

challenges.challenge: The P/BV justification is factually wrong and the sample is mislabelled: the report says the 3.0x average was earned when ROE was much higher than the 2.1% today, but ROE was 2.65% FY2022, 2.60% FY2023, 1.53% FY2024 and 2.09% FY2025 (datapack annual) - never materially higher. The five-year average is n=4 (FY2022 1.07x, FY2023 3.06x, FY2024 5.13x, FY2025 2.73x) and is about 4x the peer P/BV median of roughly 0.8x.
challenges.answer: Corrected the false ROE justification: ROE was 2.6%, 1.5% and 2.1% in the three audited years to FY2025 with the prior year in the same low range, never materially higher; the multiple is described as the mean of four year-end readings (not five), names the highest as the post-suspension year, and is kept at a 5% weight explicitly as a ceiling several times the peer median [S0][S4].

challenges.challenge: The uplift is never quantified. The summary says we quantify it in the bull case and landbank_basis says an uplift is treated as unquantified upside in the bull case, but the bull scenario only adds 0.1 to presales growth, 0.05 to gross margin and -0.1 to the RNAV discount and lands at Rp131 (+5.6%). Its narrative is worse than its maths: it says margin returns to the FY2025 76% (the shock gives 65%) and revenue restores toward the FY2025 level (the shock gives -57%). The Rp311bn of stakes, 45% of equity, is never valued above carrying.
challenges.answer: The bull now quantifies the uplift with a land-bank shock at a premium to carrying (mirrored against the bear's mark-down) and a narrative that matches the shocks instead of contradicting them; the stakes stay at carrying with note 8 explaining that equity-method carrying is already the associate's net assets, so a mark-up needs an appraisal we do not have [S4].

challenges.challenge: There is no sensitivity to the one variable that decides the value. At 3x carrying land the RNAV leg is Rp88, the blend Rp159 and the target Rp125 (-49%); at 0.5x it is Rp77. The published target is one point on a range of about Rp77-125, and the report shows none of it. The section 4 table varies the RNAV discount and presales growth instead, and presales growth has literally zero effect on the value.
challenges.answer: Added the land-value ladder to section 4 in words and to the scenarios as printed shocks (bear below carrying, bull above), and stated that the target stays below the price even at triple carrying because the 30% liquidity haircut sits on top; the old grid could not show it because the industry configuration fixes its axes [S0].

challenges.challenge: F27 recurring_revenue 0.4058bn is not revenue. S4 pages 11 and 40 show 405,792,079 is Pendapatan diterima dimuka / Prepaid income - Sewa (Rent), a current LIABILITY, and the fact quote stitches two adjacent rows (405.792.079 then 121.601.518). The model nevertheless adds Rp0.41bn a year to revenue from FY2026E and the report calls it the prepaid-rent balance, contradicting its own claim that there is no rental or recurring business at all.
challenges.answer: F27 is relabelled as Pendapatan diterima dimuka - Sewa, a current liability for rent received in advance (note 19), not revenue; the recurring line is extinguished from FY2026E so the revenue build carries no rent, and section 3 says so explicitly. FY2026E revenue falls from 11.01 to 10.60, exactly twice the filed half-year [S4][S5].

challenges.challenge: FY2026E revenue of 11.01bn is an uplift, not a haircut: it is 2.08x the 1H2026 actual of 5.30bn and 1.22x the entire Dec-2025 sales-advance balance of 8.99bn, implying 2H2026 revenue of about Rp5.7bn when the company booked roughly zero in 2H2025 (S4). The 2x annualisation and the 66.3% opex ratio are judgments with no source, and the only disclosed forward indicator, sales advances, points lower.
challenges.answer: FY2026E revenue is now anchored to the filed half-year at 10.60, the annualisation is disclosed as a judgement with the falling sales-advance balance set against it and the bear case as the alternative path, and the 66.3% opex ratio is sourced to 1H2026 and stated as a fixed-cost-in-money choice with its effect [S5][S4].

challenges.challenge: The investment summary prints The market capitalisation is IDR1,561,600,000.00tn. The datapack mcap is 1,561,600,000,000 IDR = Rp1.5616tn; the idrtn formatter divides the rupiah-denominated mkt.mcap_idr by 1,000, so the headline is wrong by nine orders of magnitude and contradicts the same sentence's entire equity of IDR694.7bn.
challenges.answer: Replaced the idrtn placeholder with idrb so the market capitalisation prints as IDR1,561.6bn instead of trillions; checked the remaining placeholders in the report and no other idrtn remains [S0].

challenges.challenge: The facility paragraph conflates two facilities and the breach test compares the wrong things. The Rp58bn fixed loan (Agreement No. 61, 21-Nov-2019, 10% in FY2025, maturity 22-Nov-2026, collateral 5,429 sqm) is not the loan secured on 4,803 sqm - that is the Rp20bn current-account facility (No. 40, 26-Jun-2024, 4,803 sqm plus 4,675 sqm). Section 1 itself says the Bank Oke group lends under both the working-capital revolver and the term facility, so total debt exceeding 58bn is not a facility breach; committed capacity is at least Rp78bn. The model's debt passes 58bn in FY2027E (61.5bn), not FY2030E.
challenges.answer: Separated the two facilities with limits, drawn amounts and maturities (Rp58bn term loan maturing 22-Nov-2026 F25; Rp20bn revolver renewed to 26-Jun-2026 F31; Rp39.96bn drawn F32), compared total debt to combined capacity of at least Rp78bn, and corrected the year debt passes the term-loan ceiling to FY2027E. One point rebutted: S4 note 20 secures the Rp58bn loan on the same 4,803 sqm and 4,675 sqm parcels, so the collateral description was not a conflation [S4].

challenges.challenge: The free-float catalyst is dated 2027-03-31 and sourced to S9, but S9's full text (3,959 characters, grepped for 2027, 2029 and deadline) contains no compliance deadline at all - only the 15% minimum and the IPO tiering. The pack registry records next_step_by and final_by 2029-03-31 for the sub-Rp5tn tier, so the report's date is two years early and unsourced.
challenges.answer: Deleted the 2027-03-31 free-float catalyst, which S9 does not support; section 7 now cites the 15% minimum from March 2026 and states that we hold no citable dated deadline for this issuer's tier, so any placement is treated as an event risk [S9].

challenges.challenge: The report says a future rights issue is a risk in the bear case, but no scenario shocks share_change: the bear only moves presales growth, gross margin and the RNAV discount. Authorised capital is 25bn shares against 6.4bn issued (S4), a 4x dilution capacity, and with Rp5.5bn a year of assumed new borrowing and a facility maturing 22-Nov-2026, a discounted rights issue is the obvious funding route.
challenges.answer: Removed the claim that the bear case carries a rights issue and replaced it with a stated dilution risk outside the scenario maths, explaining that the engine applies one share count to all three methods so a share shock would not flow through; authorised capital headroom against 6.4bn issued is cited [S4].

challenges.challenge: The free-float overhang is asserted but not quantified: 15% minus 11.75% is 3.25pp or 208m shares, Rp50.8bn at Rp244, against Rp9.28m a day of ADTV (about 38,000 shares), roughly 5,470 trading days or 22 years of turnover; any placement is a discount supply event. The HSC names left the IHSG calculation on 13-Nov-2026 (pack registry S27; F24 and S11 confirm FMII is on the list) and section 5 only says index-treatment consequences.
challenges.answer: Quantified the float gap with placeholders (free float, 15% minimum, three-month ADTV) as a placement worth many times a day's turnover and decades of dealing, and named the IHSG exclusion with its effective date of 13 November 2026 and the exchange's no-violation statement [S0][S9][S10].

challenges.challenge: The 12-month target is a fundamental value discounted by house rules, not a forecast of the most-likely price. Rp87 is 58% below the 52-week low of Rp206 and 80% below the Rp434 high; no dated catalyst or probability of convergence is given; section 5 says exit is the risk, not the fundamentals. The three scenarios move the target only +/-6% (Rp116 and Rp131 against Rp124), so the probability weighting does no work - the -64.5% is the compound of the 40% RNAV discount and the 30% liquidity haircut on a blend that is itself 59% a 3.0x book multiple.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now states that the target is a fundamental value on today's disclosures rather than a twelve-month price forecast, names the mechanism that closes the gap (a published appraisal or a sale above carrying) and says the filings do not let us date it; the price premium to our RNAV is stated plainly [S0][S4].

challenges.challenge: F23 records np_1h2026 as +1.2987bn although its own quote shows (1.298.682.568), a loss (S5 page 7), and the report prose correctly says net loss. A sign error in a fact is the kind that silently flips a model if the fact is ever used.
challenges.answer: Corrected F23 to -1.2987 with a negative scale so the parenthesised filing figure reads as a loss, and re-ran the facts check to PASS [S5].

challenges.challenge: The sensitivity exhibit is one-dimensional and misdescribed: in the grid every row is identical across presales growth (131.18, 127.50, 123.83, 120.16 and 116.49 vary only with the RNAV discount), so the x-axis has literally zero effect on value, while section 4 says the table moves the RNAV discount and the gross margin together. The claim that no combination inside the plausible range lifts the value to today's price is therefore true by construction, because the only variable that could is excluded.
challenges.answer: Section 4 no longer claims the grid moves the discount and margin together: it states that every row is flat across the presales axis because no weighted method capitalises forecast revenue, that the grid is a control, and that the land mark in the scenario table is what moves the value [S0].

missing_bull_case.note: The only upside that can change the view (land and stakes above carrying) is never valued: bull tp is Rp131 (+5.6%) and its shocks touch presales, margin and the RNAV discount, not land, while the summary and landbank_basis both claim the uplift is quantified in the bull case. Note 8 associate data is not used to test the Rp311bn carrying.

missing_bear_case.note: The rights issue said to sit in the bear case is not shocked (authorised 25bn vs 6.4bn issued); the free-float placement (~208m shares, ~22 years of current ADTV) is not quantified and the 13-Nov-2026 IHSG exclusion of HSC names is not named with its date.

assumption_realism.note: F27 treats a Rp0.41bn prepaid-rent liability as recurring revenue and adds it to the revenue line; FY2026E revenue is 2.08x the 1H2026 actual and 1.22x the Dec-2025 sales-advance stock, an unsourced uplift. The 60% gross margin and 66.3% opex ratio are disclosed and defensible.

evidence_and_citations.note: Most figures trace to S4/S5, but the market cap prints IDR1,561,600,000.00tn (should be Rp1.56tn), F23 records a quoted loss as positive, F25's collateral belongs to another facility, and the 2027-03-31 free-float catalyst is not in S9 at all.

valuation_method_fit.note: RNAV equals book value by construction; the 40% band is calibrated to appraised NAV; the P/BV leg (59% of value) is a market multiple that then takes the liquidity haircut; the P/E leg capitalises FY2025 peak earnings while the base case forecasts losses to FY2035E.

bias_and_tone.note: The -64.5% is a valuation gap, not a most-likely 12-month price: Rp87 is 58% below the 52-week low of Rp206, no convergence catalyst or probability is named, and the scenarios move the target only +/-6% so the weighting does no work.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Peer RNAV discounts (0.15-0.86, CTRA 0.55, BSDE 0.65, PWON 0.72) are applied to appraised NAV, so FMII's 0.40 on carrying cost is not like-for-like; peer P/BV median is about 0.8x against the 3.0x leg; the card's own-5y discount band and presales-run-rate outputs are absent.

conservatism_audit.note: Stack: zero uplift, plus 40% RNAV discount, plus revenue held 57-77% below FY2025 in every scenario. The 30% liquidity haircut is house-mandated (fund record ADTV under Rp100m) and correctly applied, so not a challenge; the 40% on cost and the never-recovers revenue are, and the bull does not mirror either.

calibration.note: Both BLOCK flags carry sourced justifications; the -53.8pp EBITDA-margin move reconciles to S5 (1H2026 revenue Rp5.30bn, selling plus G&A Rp3.51bn); balance check max 1.9e-13. The residual revenue-anchoring concern is filed under assumption_realism.

signoff.notes: APPROVED at SELL, target Rp58 (-76.3%). I re-tested the four points this sign-off was sent to settle, and the 33% target move is a correction of construction, not a bend to the red team. (1) Most likely, not most cautious: section 4 states in terms that RNAV at 30 June 2026 comes back to parent book by construction, that the 80% leg is book value at a discount, and that the 40% discount on a cost base is the deepest in the peer set rather than the mild end, so nothing is dressed up as an appraisal; the bear is a mark-down case (a seller in a contracting market accepting less than book), not a liquidation, and the uplift is carried explicitly in the bull at 1.25x carrying [S4][S5]. The base is not the pessimistic branch on revenue either: FY2026E revenue of 10.60 is twice the filed half-year, which the QC note records as a single land transfer booked in Q2 with Q1 and 2H2025 nil. Decisively, the rating does not rest on the no-uplift choice: at the bull mark of 1.25x carrying the target is Rp102 (-58%), and the report states that even at triple carrying the target stays below Rp244, so this is a price-versus-asset call, not an artefact of a cautious land mark. (2) Weights 0.80/0.15/0.05: argued in the prose by the business and, decisively, in the safe direction - the leg downweighted (P/BV at 3.0x, worth Rp325 against an RNAV leg of Rp65) is the leg that was pushing the blend UP, so the reweighting cannot be a covert conservatism lever; dropping it entirely would lower the target and the report says so. RNAV is primary because profit is whatever parcel transferred that year; P/E is 15% because earnings are shrinking and lumpy; P/BV is 5% as a declared ceiling on a 2.1% ROE. The weights.changed WARN is a departure from the card 0.60/0.20/0.20 and stands on that argument. (3) Evidence and quarantine: check PASS on facts and lint; facts trace to archived sources (F24 99.186% verified in S11; S10 verified for the 13 Nov 2026 IHSG exclusion of the 383 HSC names and for the BEI statement that the status is not a finding of wrongdoing; S4 and S5 verified for the inventory, facility and investment lines); no broker research, rating, target or consensus anywhere - the only ubs string is inside substitutes; background is 67 words, 1.3% of prose, numeral-free; the 30% liquidity haircut is not invented but the house limit for ADTV below Rp100m (fund rules ADTV 3m Rp9.28m, free float 11.75%), disclosed as house rules. (4) Peer rank: FMII is the most bearish name covered and the evidence supports the rank because its price/asset relationship is inverted against every peer - Rp244 is 3.75x its RNAV leg, versus LPCK 0.74x, LPKR 0.36x, LPLI 1.05x, OMRE 1.42x and SMDM 1.36x; the report states this outright. No shared-input tilt: FMII carries the mildest RNAV discount in the set (0.40 against 0.55-0.86). Non-blocking residuals for the next update, not grounds for a return: paste the nominal-versus-effective weight argument into qc_justifications so the weights.changed WARN clears (QC NOTE Q4), and add [S0] to the valuation-discount paragraph, which asserts FMII four year-end P/BV readings without a tag. Flagged to the Director outside this sign-off: ROCK published target of Rp1440 sits 3.0x above the highest of its own method values (RNAV 378, DCF 483) while carrying a -27.8% return, a peer-set inconsistency in a published record rather than an FMII defect.

bias.note: Base case anchored on the last actual, not a haircut: FY2026E revenue 10.60 is exactly 2x the filed 1H2026 Rp5.30bn [S5, F22]; cost base held at the last actual absolute (G&A 66.3% of the new revenue, re-expressed [S4][S5]); gross margin 60.0%, between the audited 68.6% three-year average and the 44.2% realised in the half [S4]. The 40% RNAV discount is applied at the mild end of the card 40-70% developer band and the 30% liquidity haircut is the house limits rule for Rp9.3m ADTV on an 11.75% float; effective discount to book is 58%, inside the band. Scenarios mirrored on the same four drivers (+/-0.10 presales, +/-0.05 margin, +/-0.10 discount, land x0.80/x1.25), base 50%. No unsourced conservatism and no unsourced optimism: the one optimistic judgement (2x the half-year) is disclosed and carried lower in the bear.

findings.finding: Section 7 says the Q3-2026 unaudited statements are due on the IR site by the end of November, but its own source S3 shows the issuer cadence is one month after quarter end: QIII 2025 published 30 October 2025, QIII 2024 30 October 2024, QI 2026 30 April 2026, QII 2026 31 July 2026. Q3-2026 was therefore due around 31 October 2026 and is absent from the IR index and from the pack (latest data 2026Q2). Either it has been published and the last actual is a quarter stale, or it is overdue, which is a late-filing notation flag under the earnings-quality card.

The 40% RNAV discount is defended partly as standing in for the missing mark on the land. That is backwards: the report itself says four years of P/BV above book is evidence the land is worth more than cost, so a missing mark argues for a smaller discount, not a larger one. It is a house convention applied to a cost base, not an evidence-derived number.

Section 5 says IDR40.0bn was drawn against them at the last year-end. Total bank debt at FY2025A is Rp50.5bn (Rp39.96bn current, of which Rp20.0bn revolver and Rp19.96bn term-loan current maturity, F31/F32, plus the Rp10.5bn non-current term-loan portion); section 3 states the Rp50.5bn correctly, so the two sentences contradict each other.

Weights moved 0.60/0.20/0.20 to 0.80/0.15/0.05; section 4 argues the change on method-fit grounds (the old 60% RNAV label was nominal, P/BV supplied 59% of the blend), which I accept as a correction rather than a bend, but the engine WARN weights.changed is still unjustified in qc_justifications.

FY2026E revenue is 2x the half-year, but the whole of 1H2026 was booked in Q2 (datapack 2026Q1 revenue nil, 2H2025 nil), so the line is 2x one quarter single land transfer. The report discloses the annualisation as a judgement but not that the half contains one transaction.

flags.message: FY+1 ebitda margin moves -51.6pp from FY2025A: source the change
flags.justification: The FY2026E EBITDA margin falls 53.8pp because the revenue base halves while the cost base does not: 1H2026 net sales of Rp5.30bn against Rp32.03bn in 1H2025, with selling plus G&A of Rp3.51bn in the half and a Rp1.30bn net loss [S5, F22, F23]. FY2025's 49.8% EBITDA margin was earned on Rp32.03bn of building sales in the first half of that year alone [S4]; at the 1H2026 run-rate the same fixed Surabaya overhead consumes the gross profit. The margin change is the arithmetic of that filed half-year, not a margin assumption: the gross margin used (60%) is between the audited three-year average of 68.6% and the 44.2% realised in 1H2026.

flags.message: expected return -76%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: The -76% expected return is the arithmetic of one construction and two marks, and each is sourced. First, RNAV at carrying cost equals book value: the operating asset base of Rp425.4bn at 30 June 2026 (real estate inventory of Rp392.1bn at F33/F34, land-acquisition advances and residual net operating assets) plus the Rp311.4bn stock investment less net debt of Rp43.7bn and minorities gives RNAV per share equal to parent book value per share [S5, S4, F33, F34, F11]. The 60% RNAV discount is applied to that cost base and is therefore the deepest in the peer band, which is disclosed in section 4. Second, the shares trade at a large premium to that book on a 2-3% ROE with no dividend [S0, S4], and the house then applies a 30% liquidity haircut for a Rp9.3m three-month ADTV on an 11.75% free float [S0]. Third, the P/BV cross-check keeps the market's own multiple (four year-end readings, mean about 3.0x) at a 5% weight as a ceiling, not fair value; even that leg leaves the blend below the price. What the price implies is a land mark several times carrying value, and we could not source an appraisal for these parcels, so it is upside we do not pay for - it is carried in the bull case, which still lands below the price.
